title: Finding the Topic of Each Post
statement:
A site wants to tag its posts with topics:

- `Keywords(topic_id, word)`: each row says that `word` expresses topic `topic_id`. `(topic_id, word)` is unique. A topic can have several words, and the same word can belong to several topics.
- `Posts(post_id, content)`: one row per post; `post_id` is unique. `content` is words of English letters separated by single spaces.

A post has a topic when one of that topic's keywords appears in its content as a **whole word**, ignoring letter case (`WAR` matches `war`, but `war` does not match `warning`).

For every post report `post_id` and `topic`: the post's topic ids in ascending numeric order, each once, joined with commas and no spaces (for example `1,3`), or the text `Ambiguous!` when the post has no topic. Rows may come in any order.
constraints: (topic_id, word) is unique in Keywords, ignoring case
word is one word of English letters
content is words of English letters separated by single spaces
reference:
WITH matches AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT p.post_id, k.topic_id
  FROM Posts AS p
  JOIN Keywords AS k
    ON CONCAT(' ', LOWER(p.content), ' ') LIKE CONCAT('% ', LOWER(k.word), ' %')
)
SELECT p.post_id,
       IFNULL(GROUP_CONCAT(m.topic_id ORDER BY m.topic_id), 'Ambiguous!') AS topic
FROM Posts AS p
LEFT JOIN matches AS m
  ON m.post_id = p.post_id
GROUP BY p.post_id;
brute:
SELECT p.post_id,
       IFNULL(
         (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT k.topic_id ORDER BY k.topic_id SEPARATOR ',')
          FROM Keywords AS k
          WHERE p.content REGEXP CONCAT('(^| )', k.word, '( |$)')),
         'Ambiguous!'
       ) AS topic
FROM Posts AS p

Posts: We call it soccer They call it football hahaha
Americans prefer basketball while Europeans love handball and football
stop the war and play handball
warning I planted some flowers this morning and then got vaccinated
stop the war and play handball

notes:
## Intuition

A keyword counts only as a whole word, and letter case does not matter. Lower-case both sides and pad the content with a space at each end: then every word of the post, including the first and the last, sits between two spaces, so `' war '` occurs in `' stop the war and play handball '` but not in `' warning i planted ... '`. One `LIKE` per (post, keyword) pair decides the match. After that it is grouping: collect each post's distinct topic ids in order, and fall back to `Ambiguous!` when there are none.

## Approach

1. `matches`: join `Posts` (`p`) to `Keywords` (`k`) on `' ' + content + ' '` containing `' ' + word + ' '`, both lower-cased, and keep `DISTINCT` (post, topic) pairs, since two keywords of one topic may both appear.
2. Start again from `Posts` and `LEFT JOIN matches` (`m`), so posts without any topic survive with a null `topic_id`.
3. Group by post and build `GROUP_CONCAT(m.topic_id ORDER BY m.topic_id)`; its default separator is a comma.
4. `IFNULL(..., 'Ambiguous!')`: a post whose only row has a null topic concatenates to null.

## Example 1, step by step

- Post 1 contains `' football '`, so `matches` holds (1, 1).
- Post 2 contains `' handball '` and `' football '`, both topic 1; `DISTINCT` keeps one (2, 1).
- Post 3 contains `' war '` (keyword `WAR`, topic 3) and `' handball '` (topic 1): (3, 1) and (3, 3), joined as `1,3`.
- Post 4 has `warning` and `vaccinated` but neither `' war '` nor `' vaccine '`, so it has no match and becomes `Ambiguous!`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(P · K · L) for P posts, K keywords and content length L, because every pair is tested with `LIKE`; grouping adds O(P + matches).
- Space: O(P · T) for `matches` with T topics.

## Pitfalls

- `LIKE CONCAT('%', word, '%')` without spaces matches inside longer words, so `war` would tag `warning`.
- Padding only one side misses a keyword at the start or end of the content.
- Without `DISTINCT` a topic matched by two keywords appears twice, as in `1,1`.
- An inner join drops posts with no topic instead of reporting `Ambiguous!`.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `p` | a post |
| `k` | a keyword whose padded word occurs in the padded content |
| `matches` | distinct (post_id, topic_id) pairs found |
| `m` | a post's matches; null for a post with none |
| `topic` | sorted topic ids joined by commas, or `Ambiguous!` |

narration.1: The first stage finds which topics each post mentions.
narration.2: DISTINCT keeps one row per post and topic even when several keywords of that topic appear.
narration.4: Every post is tested against every keyword.
narration.5: Padding the lower-cased content and keyword with spaces makes LIKE match whole words only, wherever they sit.
narration.8: Topic ids are joined in ascending order with commas; a post with no match concatenates to null and becomes Ambiguous!.
narration.10: A left join keeps posts that matched no keyword.
